plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs time-to-event, adjusted for case/control
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 60-case vs 60-control human tumor-biopsy bulk RNA-seq cohort (n=120, gene-level Salmon counts, 12000 genes) with a follow-up time and event indicator per sample and a 20-gene signature list. The research question is whether the signature score is associated with time-to-event once case/control status is accounted for. The plan: (1) QC the sample structure on variance-stabilized counts; (2) filter and normalize the counts (filterByExpr + TMM, following the population-cohort rule for n>=50/group, which flags that DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial models exaggerate false positives at this sample size); (3) score every sample on the 20-gene signature with UCell, a rank-based, per-sample method that does not depend on the other samples in the batch; (4) fit a Cox proportional hazards model of time-to-event on the standardized signature score with case/control status as a covariate (the exact 'once we account for' adjustment the question asks for), check the proportional-hazards assumption via scaled Schoenfeld residuals, and report the hazard ratio per SD with its 95% CI; (5) compute a time-dependent ROC/AUC at clinically meaningful horizons as a discrimination readout, since a plain ROC on the event indicator would mishandle censoring; (6) as a secondary robustness step, test whether the score differs between the case and control groups themselves (limma/t-test on the score) so that a positive Cox association can be interpreted with awareness of collinearity between the score and the case/control label; (7) synthesize into one report with the reproducibility record (package versions, thresholds, signature provenance). No enrichment or DE gene-list analysis was requested by the user beyond the signature itself, so DE/pathway steps are omitted as unasked scope — the signature score is the sole feature under test. The `survival` R package itself is not listed as importable in the environment census; `rms::cph` (rms 8.1-1, present) and `timeROC` (0.4.1, present) implement the same Cox/Schoenfeld/time-dependent-AUC methodology and are used as substitutes, noted explicitly as such.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If each group holds 50 or more samples, use limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model for the differential expression test. In a population cohort the sample-to-sample variation does not obey the negative binomial model, and DESeq2 and edgeR then report many false positives, even on permuted labels. The linear model on the log counts with precision weights keeps the false discovery rate closer to the nominal level than the count models, but it also exceeds it on some data. The paper recommends the Wilcoxon rank-sum test at a large sample size. State this caution in the report, and give the Wilcoxon test or a permutation check as the control.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
